title: Forensic analysis shows latest Chinese LLMs were trained on Nvidia Blackwell B200/B300
gist: A SemiWiki forum post relays a claim by will depue (@willdepue) of conclusive forensic evidence that DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group trained their newest models (Deepseek-V4, Kimi K3, MiniMax-M3, Ling-3.1) on export-controlled Nvidia Blackwell GPUs, based on GPU-specific patterns in open-weight initial values. The quoted estimate puts the largest runs at 2,000-3,000 Blackwell GPUs each and over half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs across these labs; the poster notes the claim reads with some sensationalism.

themes.theme: Forensic claim of Blackwell use by Chinese labs

insights.claim: A post by will depue claims conclusive forensic evidence that the top four Chinese AI labs, DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group, built their newest models (Deepseek-V4, Kimi K3, MiniMax-M3 and Ling-3.1) on Nvidia Blackwell chips that are barred from export to China.
insights.speaker: K
insights.so_what: If substantiated, it implies widespread export-control evasion and could trigger tighter enforcement affecting Nvidia's China-related sales channels.
insights.quote: the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China
insights.locator: I have a major result to share.

insights.claim: The poster notes the claim reads with a bit of sensationalism, framing it as a third-party assertion rather than independently verified.
insights.speaker: K
insights.so_what: Treat as an unverified signal pending corroboration before pricing policy risk.

insights.claim: The method rests on the idea that a model's base seed or starting weight values follow a pattern established by the GPU it is trained on, so open weights compared against reference data from different GPUs can reveal which GPU trained a model.
insights.speaker: K
insights.so_what: Hardware fingerprinting of open-weight models could become an export-control enforcement tool, raising compliance risk for labs and chip resellers.

themes.theme: Scale and cost of export-controlled compute

insights.claim: The quoted estimate is that Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro each used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs, with clusters of that size costing about $150 to $200 million each.
insights.speaker: K
insights.so_what: Sizes the gray-market flow of frontier GPUs into China at meaningful dollar levels.
insights.quote: I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each
